user.title: Energy Management System
user.description: Configure the energy sources used to decide when appliances may run.

data.debug_log: Write full debug log to ems_debug.log

data_description.solar_production_sensor: Sensor reporting solar production in watts (required).
data_description.house_load_sensor: Optional sensor reporting total house load in watts.
data_description.grid_export_sensor: Optional net grid power sensor (watts): positive when importing, negative when exporting. The exported (negative) part becomes the surplus budget; preferred over the solar minus house-load estimate.
data_description.peak_tariff_sensor: Binary sensor that is on during peak-tariff hours.
data_description.voltage: Voltage (or a number entity) used to convert watts to amps. Defaults to 230 V.
data_description.demand_power_current_peak_sensor: Sensor reporting the running average power over the current 15-minute quarter. Enables the quarterly-demand sensors.
data_description.demand_power_consumed_sensor: Sensor reporting current power consumption, used to project demand to the end of the quarter.
data_description.demand_month_max_sensor: Sensor reporting the highest quarter-hour demand recorded this month. Required for the quarterly-demand sensors.
data_description.minimal_peak_warning: Floor for the monthly peak in kW (e.g. 4). The limits never drop below this.
data_description.peak_high_safety: kW subtracted from the monthly peak to set the High limit (e.g. 0.4).
data_description.peak_critical_safety: kW subtracted from the monthly peak to set the Critical limit (e.g. 0.2).
data_description.cost_peak: Sensor or number entity with the price you pay per kWh imported during peak hours. Leave empty to use the default (0.40 €/kWh).
data_description.cost_offpeak: Sensor or number entity with the price you pay per kWh imported during off-peak hours. Leave empty to use the default (0.20 €/kWh).
data_description.gain_peak: Sensor or number entity with what you receive per kWh exported during peak hours; leave empty for the default (0.10 €/kWh). Read every cycle, so dynamic tariffs work. Together with the two import prices it drives the off_peak-mode breakeven decision.
data_description.gain_offpeak: Sensor or number entity with what you receive per kWh exported during off-peak hours; leave empty for the default (0.10 €/kWh). Use the same entity as the peak one when your contract pays a single injection price.

data_description.priority: Lower numbers run first when surplus is limited.
data_description.min_amps: Minimum amps the appliance needs to run.
data_description.max_amps: Maximum amps the appliance may draw.
data_description.fixed_amps: Number entity ('ampere to use') the optimizer sets based on available excess; its own min/max become the appliance's amp limits.
data_description.fixed_amps_hysteresis_seconds: Minimum time the amps setpoint is held before it may change again.
data_description.power_sensor: Optional sensor reporting the appliance's real power draw (W); used for budgeting instead of an estimate.
data_description.partial_min_excess: Minimum averaged excess required to run in partial_solar mode.
data_description.connected_sensor: Optional binary sensor; the appliance is skipped while it is off.
data_description.ev_soc_sensor: Optional. State-of-charge sensor (%) of the car this charger serves. Setting it makes the appliance an EV charger: while the car is plugged in (connected sensor on) and its SoC is below the 'Force charge below' threshold, it charges from the grid as in forced mode (peak protection still applies). An unknown/unavailable SoC never forces.
data_description.hysteresis_on_off_seconds: Minimum time an on/off state is held before it may change, to prevent rapid cycling.
data_description.averaging_window_seconds: Window over which excess power is averaged.
